text: Today's adornment: Sri Lalita Tripura Sundari Devi
Today, Kanakadurgamma on Indrakeeladri in Vijayawada gives darshan as Sri Lalita Tripura Sundari Devi.
In the Srividya tradition, the Mother Goddess is worshipped as Parashakti.
In her hands are a noose, an ankus, a sugarcane bow, and flower arrows.
The Lalita Sahasranama itself tells the meaning behind the bow and arrows—
It describes the mind as a sugarcane bow.
It describes the five subtle elements that are the source of sound, touch, form, taste, and smell as arrows.
That means, the mind through which we understand the world, and sensory experiences, have also been shown to be connected with the Mother Goddess's form.
In the Mother Goddess's form, not only is there beauty,
but also the wisdom to understand our inner self.
Om Sri Lalita Tripura Sundaryai Namah ॥
